title: Palette follow-up: bring back vibrant colours and stop consumers depending on cycle order
user-messages: ok ui-17 is good for now, make a ticket to think more about this in the future and get the more vibrant colors back, and also the ticekt would fix that there still a little bit of leaking of the data model into the consumers cause they have to know about the order of the pallettes in the cycles in some instances
definition-of-done:
1. The default palette is at least as vibrant as master before UI-17, shown by side-by-side screenshots of the menu, knot editor, code pane, DSL graph, model scenes and trade scene.
2. No consumer reads a palette cycle by a position that carries meaning; reordering any cycle in Palettes.java changes no scene's role-to-colour mapping.
3. Every palette in Palettes still works in every scene, and PaletteRolesTest passes.
4. Swapping palettes recolours baked overlays and cached text without a reload.
testing-plan:
1. Screenshot every scene under every palette with tmp/palette_shots.sh and compare against pre-UI-17 master shots.
2. A test that permutes each cycle of a palette and checks the named roles consumers use still resolve to the same colours.
3. PaletteRolesTest and the full suite.
todos: Trade game under the shared palette (TRADE-24 on UI-17): in PAPER the river is saturated BLUE_TEAL_DARK, the loop bar's cargo segment bright purple and roads dark grey; in SLATE the river is cream and the moor matches the grid lines; the fogged rival pipe nearly vanishes in DARK/SLATE. Screenshots: Ixdar trade-24 worktree tmp/trade24-palette-*.png
unknowns: Whether vibrancy comes from retuning DARK, adding a VIVID palette, or adding fields (e.g. a second accent)
Whether category colours become named fields or an unordered cycle, and how the GLSL vector components x/y/z/w keep stable colours
